title: Scalar types (resolved release file)
description: dist/scalars.json: every type fully resolved. Nothing here needs code to read: no inheritance, no references.

checks.description: Every check a type's check may name, with its exact meaning. A check runs on the normalized value after the pattern matched.

errors.description: The message template of each error code a models engine reports. {name} is replaced by the problem's param of that name. A code with no template (a reason from $meta.reasons, other than too_long) takes the type's error as its message.

lookup.description: How to find a type from a word a person typed.

reasons.description: Why a validate failed, in the order the single pass checks: a value that breaks several rules gets the first. Every language's ScalarError carries one, and models report it as the problem's code.

normalize_steps.description: Every cleanup step a type's normalize list may name, with its exact meaning.

params.description: Every setting a field can take (length, precision, values, ...), defined once. A type's params lists the ones it accepts; nullable applies to every type.

postgres_attrs.description: Settings only Postgres has, defined once. A type's postgres.attr lists the ones it accepts; collation applies to every text and varchar column.

primitive.description: The basic type this one is built from: the only thing a language needs to map to a native type.

alternative.description: For advanced and domain types: the core type to use instead.

schema.description: The rule, as plain JSON Schema keywords: pass it to any JSON Schema validator.

pattern.description: Anchored ^...$ and limited to a subset every common engine reads the same (Go, Python, Rust, JS, Postgres): no \d \s \w, no '.', no lookaround or backreferences. In Python use re.fullmatch: '$' alone also matches before a trailing newline.

minLength.description: Fewest characters, counted as Unicode code points.

maxLength.description: Most characters, counted as Unicode code points.

check.description: A name from $meta.checks: a rule beyond the pattern, like a check digit or a 64-bit range. JSON Schema, HTML and Postgres do not run it.

params.description: Names from $meta.params that a field of this type can set.

check_invalid.description: Values that pass the pattern but fail the type's check.

check.description: A CHECK constraint enforcing the same rule as schema. Replace {column} with the quoted column name, like CHECK ("slug" ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$').
